| Output at the center | Value |

| Steered to 0 degrees, equal to G_x | 9.9993 |
| Steered to 90 degrees, equal to -G_y | -3.9997 |
| cos 30 x (0 degrees) + sin 30 x (90 degrees) | 6.6598 |

A 9 x 9 ramp with the value 10 x + 4 y, sigma 1 and the first derivative. The brightness rises by 10 per pixel along x and by 4 per pixel down, so G_x is close to 10 and G_y close to 4. They come out slightly low, because the Gaussian is cut at 4 sigma. The direction at 90 degrees points up, so that output is -G_y. Mixing the outputs at 0 and 90 degrees with cos 30 and sin 30 gives the output at 30 degrees, which is the steering rule. The strongest response is the length of (G_x, G_y), and its angle, atan2(-G_y, G_x), points toward the brightest side, down and to the right.
